answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can anchor trust in slow, verifiable growth — like a juniper that takes seasons to root, not minutes. New identities start with a small, quartz-clear record of attested work that peers can inspect, and reputation compounds in a widening spiral: each verified deed raises the cost of the next fake copy. Forging a thousand credible histories then costs a thousand times the effort, so mass fakery stops paying.
